rule: Byte and count budgets set their limit at most 20 percent above the measured baseline, so a 20 percent regression fails CI. Time budgets run on shared hosted runners with software rendering, so each declares a headroom factor of at most 3 and a reason, takes the fastest of several samples and asserts at one RTT only. Manual budgets are measured by hand and recorded as result files. See docs/adr/0154-performance-budget-file-and-regression-rule.md.

budgets.measures: One POST of 10,000 cell annotations to the bulk annotation endpoint, from the request to the 201, one sample
budgets.headroomReason: The baseline is the whole test call on the last green hosted run, so it is an upper bound of the request. On a busy hosted runner, where the whole db job ran 1.43 times slower, the request alone took 6488 ms, 1.8 times the baseline, with no change in its path. The test keeps one 10,000 row sample because three would triple it, so 2.5 times covers a busy runner and still fails a doubling on a quiet one.
budgets.environment: GitHub hosted ubuntu runner, PostGIS 17 service container, FastAPI test client in process, so no network RTT
